chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is recommended that you recite at the end of the forenoon on Friday, Surah Al-Rahman in its entirety.'
Then you should say, every time you recite 'Which then of the Favours of your Lord will you two deny?', 'There is nothing from Your Favours, Lord, that I deny.'

key_terms.فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ: Which then of the Favours of your Lord will you two deny? (Quran 55:13)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended recitation and response for Surah Al-Rahman on Friday according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights a specific Friday devotional practice where reciting the entirety of Surah Al-Rahman serves as a comprehensive affirmation of divine blessings. The unique supplication appended to the recurring verse transforms the rhetorical question into a personal declaration of gratitude, a practice emphasized by Shia scholars to deepen spiritual connection on the holiest day of the week. This ritual underscores the theological importance of acknowledging both human and jinn faculties in recognizing God's favors.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Hammad Bin Usman who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘It is recommended that you recite at the end of the day on the day of Friday, (Surah) Al-Rahman (Chapter 55), all of it.
Then you should be saying, every time you recited [55:13] Which then of the Favours of your Lord will you two deny?, ‘There is nothing from Yourazwj Favours, Lordazwj, do I deny’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘It is preferable to recite Chapter 55 of the Holy Quran after the morning Salah (prayer) on Friday morning
and after reciting the verse that says, “Which of the bounties of your Lord do you then deny?” say, ‘I do not deny anyone of the bounties of my Lord.’”
